newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Sept 4.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Sept 4.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

U.S. film and television studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM), recently bought by a consortium comprising Seven Network and U.S. investor Kirk Kerkorian, has forecast 1996 earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) of US$75.5 million. According to The Australian Financial Review, MGM's EBIT would then fall to US$55.2 million in 1997 and then rise to US$89.5 million in 1998.
Canadian media mogul Conrad Black said late on Tuesday speculation his 25 percent stake in Australian newspaper publisher John Fairfax was on the market was false.
* The Broken Hill Pty Ltd A$17.12 (-0.08)

Oil prices in New York surged five percent overnight on the back of the latest confrontation between the United States and Iraq. Crude oil for October delivery closed up US$1.15 at US$23.40 a barrel on the New York Mercantile Exchange after rising as high as US$24.25 in early trading.
Dominion Mining Ltd said late on Tuesday it expected to make "tangible" headway toward development of its Yakabindie nickel/cobalt project in Western Australia in the next two months.
John Singleton Advertising Ltd said on Tuesday it had commissioned expert advice on a mechanism for selling down part or all of its 10 percent stake in unlisted television broadcaster TEN Group Ltd.

Diversified manufacturer Pacific BBA Ltd said on Tuesday trading conditions so far in the second half of calendar 1996 had been softer than expected and it now believed 1996 profits would be around the same level as 1995.

Dairy and fruit juice group National Foods Ltd said on Tuesday reforms announced in July were now almost fully completed and the group was poised for above-budget profit growth in the next six to nine months. The company earlier posted an annual net profit of A$15.05 million, up from A$10.77 million previously.
